final.memo:
Charlie and I have always found that the best time to be greedy is when Mr. Market is suffering from a bout of profound melancholy. Right now, the indicators are clear: we are seeing a 'death of equities' mentality that mirrors the conditions of 1974 [D03], [D06]. With a trailing earnings yield of 13.83% stacked against a ten-year Treasury yield of 8.91%, the math dictates a simple course of action: we buy [D03], [D04].

While critics point to inflation and the replacement cost of assets as reasons to stay on the sidelines, we prefer to look at the underlying business economics [D05]. We are buying claims on cash flows, not index points. When we can acquire a diversified group of businesses at a discount to book value, we are buying a margin of safety that bonds—with their fixed coupons and susceptibility to purchasing-power erosion—simply cannot match [D02], [D04]. We do not need a catalyst; we need only to deploy our capital into wonderful businesses that can maintain their competitive position regardless of the near-term economic weather [D01], [D04].
